target_customer: Advertisers, recruiters and event sponsors paying to reach Asia's tech and startup audience
problem: English language coverage of Asia's startup scene was thin, leaving founders, investors and readers without a regional source.
business_model: Media: advertising, sponsored content, jobs board and events

founders.name: Willis Wee
founders.background_notes: Started the blog as Penn Olson; per YC page he ran the company for 16 years through exit.

competitors.name: e27
competitors.what: Singapore based startup and tech blog

technical_complexity.rationale: A publishing site with editorial and events operations; the difficulty was content and distribution, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Audience and brand built over years, but any blogger could publish competing coverage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; a Singapore media group, SPH Media, bought it in late 2023.

market_need_then: A 2011 TechWire Asia piece noted Penn Olson was the only blog focused fully on Asian digital and tech, with rising startup activity in the region.

branding.name_origin: Began as the personal blog Penn Olson, where the founder said he learns by penning down his thoughts; renamed Tech in Asia.
branding.domain_note: techinasia.com used as the main domain

rebrands.why: Reason not stated in sources seen; a Japanese report gives March 2012, another source says by 2013.

branding.community_and_virality: Ran City Chapters community events and a jobs board per the 2017 funding article

brand_strength.rationale: Described as the largest English language tech media on Asia and was bought by a major publisher, but no evidence of a brand driven breakout.

outcome_analysis: Tech in Asia grew from the Penn Olson blog into the largest English language tech outlet on Asia, raised about 10 million dollars across rounds by 2017 and was acquired by SPH Media in late 2023. Reports put the price near 30 million dollars but terms were not disclosed.
notes: techinasia.com could not be fetched (blocked by tool). 2015 round was called Series C by TechCrunch and only a funding round by AVCJ, so stage is other. Acquisition price near 30M is reported by deal trackers and DealStreetAsia, not confirmed, so amount_usd is null. 2011 East Ventures date from interview summary. Founder education not found in opened sources.
